html:
The Mazahua are an Otomanguean people of central Mexico, living in the northwest of the State of Mexico and the east of Michoacán. Their language is close to Otomí.

In the 1400s their land lay between the Aztec Triple Alliance and the Purépecha kingdom, and the Aztecs conquered them and took tribute. Their neighbours included the Matlatzinca of the Toluca valley. Under Spanish rule they worked on haciendas and in mines. In the 1900s many moved to Mexico City to work, and Mazahua women selling goods in its streets became a familiar sight. In 2004 Mazahua women protested that the Cutzamala water system sent their water to the city while their own villages went short.
sum: The Mazahua are an Otomanguean people of central Mexico, living in the northwest of the State of Mexico and the east of Michoacán. Their language is close to Otomí.
